title: The Long Uniform
premise: In the final winter of a long war, Vesper Okonkwo keeps a ledger of soldiers' names that officers leave off official casualty reports, believing history happens elsewhere — until the army requisitions their town, their hospital, and the ledger itself. When Vesper discovers the ledger is to be destroyed as part of a cover-up before the armistice negotiations, they and a ragtag found family of nurses, a deserter, and a wounded enemy soldier must smuggle it past three military checkpoints. At the last checkpoint, with the armistice hours from signing, Vesper trades their own name for the ledger's survival, signing themselves into history so the omitted can be remembered.
about_author: August Okonkwo is the pen name of a former field medic turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters in military storage depots. They write historical fiction about the people paperwork forgets.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Vesper Okonkwo, a battlefield nurse at St. Ambrose convalescent hospital, records in a private ledger the names of dying soldiers omitted from official reports. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: quiet defiance disguised as routine; Vesper insists they are merely keeping accounts, not making history.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Army officers arrive and commandeer the town, the hospital, and its records for the approaching armistice logistics. Vesper hides the ledger inside a mattress of an empty bed. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dread — the abstract war becomes furniture, boots, and inventory lists in the corridors.

chapters.title: The Mattress That Walked
chapters.summary: A quartermaster's clerk nearly discovers the ledger during inventory; young nurse Adaeze covers by claiming the bed belongs to her 'brother.' POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: first bond of the found family forms through a shared lie.

chapters.title: A Deserter in the Laundry
chapters.summary: Vesper finds Corporal Ilse Brandt, a deserter from the opposing army, hiding among laundry sacks. Instead of reporting her, Vesper gives her a nurse's uniform — the long uniform of the title. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: mercy as risk; belonging begins with costume.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Vesper learns the army plans to burn all unofficial records before the armistice delegation arrives, erasing evidence of misreported casualties. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the ledger has become contraband, and Vesper has become a smuggler without choosing it.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Vesper maps the route out of town: the rail yard checkpoint, the bridge checkpoint, and the delegation gate at the old customs house. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into strategy; the deserter knows how soldiers search.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Brother
chapters.summary: The lie about Adaeze's brother unravels when a real Okonkwo relative arrives searching for family. Adaeze must decide whether to claim the stranger or protect the secret. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: found family tested against blood family.

chapters.title: The Wounded Enemy
chapters.summary: A badly wounded prisoner-of-war, Tomas, is brought in; officers order him left untreated. Vesper and Ilse treat him secretly at night. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: guilt and tenderness entwined — she treats him like everyone she failed to save.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Rail Yard
chapters.summary: Disguised as a supply run, Vesper and Adaeze carry the ledger sewn into a stretcher roll through the rail yard. A sergeant recognizes Vesper but lets them pass, owed from an old debt. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: relief laced with terror — luck is not a plan.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Kindness
chapters.summary: Major Fenwick, the requisition officer, hosts tea for the nurses and probes gently about missing records. Vesper lies fluently for the first time. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the cost of deception — Vesper realizes they are becoming someone new.

chapters.title: Tomas Speaks
chapters.summary: Tomas recovers enough to talk; he was a clerk on the other side and confirms both armies burn their ledgers. He offers to help forge transit papers. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: enemies discovering shared humanity over shared paperwork.

chapters.title: The Armistice Rumor
chapters.summary: Word spreads that the armistice may fail; fighting could resume. The hospital fills again, and the smuggling window narrows to days. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: hope curdling into urgency — peace itself becomes a deadline.

chapters.title: Ilse's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilse's own army's patrol reaches the town searching deserters. She must hide while Vesper's found family shields her, deepening her debt and her sense of home. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: the deserter stops running and starts belonging.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Bridge
chapters.summary: With forged papers by Tomas, the group crosses the bridge checkpoint, but a sentry demands to inspect the stretcher roll. Ilse creates a diversion using her own language and uniform. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely; the uniform saves them.

chapters.title: Fenwick Closes In
chapters.summary: Major Fenwick discovers the empty bed, the false brother, and the missing ledger page copied by a spy among the staff. He sets a trap at the final gate. POV: Vesper. Emotional bet: betrayal within the walls; paranoia replaces camaraderie.

chapters.title: The Spy in Ward Four
chapters.summary: The group identifies the informant — quiet Nurse Pell, coerced by threats against her son. Instead of punishing her, they feed her false information. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: compassion as tactics; even the betrayer is folded into the family.

chapters.title: False Papers, True Names
chapters.summary: Tomas forges a delegation pass, but it requires a real name that will be checked against rolls. Each member offers theirs; Vesper secretly takes the slot. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: love expressed through logistics; the ledger's keeper prepares to spend himself.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: At the delegation gate, Fenwick waits. Vesper walks through alone carrying the ledger openly, declaring it a petition of names for the armistice record. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: climax — courage as witness rather than escape.

chapters.title: The Signing Room
chapters.summary: Inside, delegates argue whether the ledger is admissible. Vesper reads names aloud until one delegate, moved, enters it into the official annex. Outside, guns fall silent — the armistice holds. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from exhaustion; history finally happens here.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Fenwick arrests Vesper for falsifying transit papers, but the signed annex makes prosecution politically impossible; Vesper is released into the crowd celebrating peace. POV: Adaeze. Emotional beat: bittersweet vindication — justice arrived sideways, as it usually does.

chapters.title: After the Guns
chapters.summary: Spring comes. The found family — Adaeze, Ilse, Tomas, even Nurse Pell — gathers in the half-empty hospital, deciding what to rebuild together. POV: Ilse. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude braided; home is now a choice, not an address.

chapters.title: The Long Uniform, Folded
chapters.summary: Vesper folds the nurse's uniform that started everything and begins a second ledger: not the dead, but the living, starting with the names of those who carried each other through. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance redefined as memory passed hand to hand, belonging written in one's own hand at last.
